metric.label: Lexical baseline
metric.description: Character n-gram cosine distance. This is a reproducible lexical baseline, not a semantic or faithfulness score.

units.leftText: The LORD’s word that came to Joel, the son of Pethuel.
units.rightText: This is the word of the LORD that came to Joel son of Pethuel:
leftNotes: 1:1 When rendered in ALL CAPITAL LETTERS, “LORD” or “GOD” is the translation of God’s Proper Name (Hebrew “יהוה*”, usually pronounced Yahweh).

units.leftText: Hear this, you elders, and listen, all you inhabitants of the land! Has this ever happened in your days, or in the days of your fathers?
units.rightText: Hear this, O elders; and give ear, all who dwell in the land. Has anything like this ever happened in your days or in the days of your fathers?

units.leftText: Tell your children about it, and have your children tell their children, and their children, another generation.
units.rightText: Tell it to your children; let your children tell it to their children, and their children to the next generation.

units.leftText: What the swarming locust has left, the great locust has eaten. What the great locust has left, the grasshopper has eaten. What the grasshopper has left, the caterpillar has eaten.
units.rightText: What the devouring locust has left, the swarming locust has eaten; what the swarming locust has left, the young locust has eaten; and what the young locust has left, the destroying locust has eaten.
rightNotes: 1:4 The precise identification of the four kinds of locusts mentioned here is uncertain.

units.leftText: Wake up, you drunkards, and weep! Wail, all you drinkers of wine, because of the sweet wine, for it is cut off from your mouth.
units.rightText: Wake up, you drunkards, and weep; wail, all you drinkers of wine, because of the sweet wine, for it has been cut off from your mouth.

units.leftText: For a nation has come up on my land, strong, and without number. His teeth are the teeth of a lion, and he has the fangs of a lioness.
units.rightText: For a nation has invaded My land, powerful and without number; its teeth are the teeth of a lion, and its fangs are the fangs of a lioness.

units.leftText: He has laid my vine waste, and stripped my fig tree. He has stripped its bark, and thrown it away. Its branches are made white.
units.rightText: It has laid waste My grapevine and splintered My fig tree. It has stripped off the bark and thrown it away; the branches have turned white. A Call to Mourning

units.leftText: Mourn like a virgin dressed in sackcloth for the husband of her youth!
units.rightText: Wail like a virgin dressed in sackcloth, grieving for the husband of her youth.

units.leftText: The meal offering and the drink offering are cut off from the LORD’s house. The priests, the LORD’s ministers, mourn.
units.rightText: Grain and drink offerings have been cut off from the house of the LORD; the priests are in mourning, those who minister before the LORD.

units.leftText: The field is laid waste. The land mourns, for the grain is destroyed, The new wine has dried up, and the oil languishes.
units.rightText: The field is ruined; the land mourns. For the grain is destroyed, the new wine is dried up, and the oil fails.

units.leftText: Be confounded, you farmers! Wail, you vineyard keepers, for the wheat and for the barley; for the harvest of the field has perished.
units.rightText: Be dismayed, O farmers, wail, O vinedressers, over the wheat and barley, because the harvest of the field has perished.

units.leftText: The vine has dried up, and the fig tree withered— the pomegranate tree, the palm tree also, and the apple tree, even all of the trees of the field are withered; for joy has withered away from the sons of men.
units.rightText: The grapevine is dried up, and the fig tree is withered; the pomegranate, palm, and apple— all the trees of the orchard— are withered. Surely the joy of mankind has dried up. A Call to Repentance (Amos 5:4–15|AMO 5:4-15*; Zephaniah 2:1–3|ZEP 2:1-3*; Luke 13:1–5|LUK 13:1-5*)

units.leftText: Put on sackcloth and mourn, you priests! Wail, you ministers of the altar. Come, lie all night in sackcloth, you ministers of my God, for the meal offering and the drink offering are withheld from your God’s house.
units.rightText: Put on sackcloth and lament, O priests; wail, O ministers of the altar. Come, spend the night in sackcloth, O ministers of my God, because the grain and drink offerings are withheld from the house of your God.

units.leftText: Sanctify a fast. Call a solemn assembly. Gather the elders and all the inhabitants of the land to the house of the LORD, your God, and cry to the LORD.
units.rightText: Consecrate a fast; proclaim a solemn assembly! Gather the elders and all the residents of the land to the house of the LORD your God, and cry out to the LORD.

units.leftText: Alas for the day! For the day of the LORD is at hand, and it will come as destruction from the Almighty.
units.rightText: Alas for the day! For the Day of the LORD is near, and it will come as destruction from the Almighty.

units.leftText: Isn’t the food cut off before our eyes, joy and gladness from the house of our God?
units.rightText: Has not the food been cut off before our very eyes — joy and gladness from the house of our God?

units.leftText: The seeds rot under their clods. The granaries are laid desolate. The barns are broken down, for the grain has withered.
units.rightText: The seeds lie shriveled beneath the clods; the storehouses are in ruins; the granaries are broken down, for the grain has withered away.

units.leftText: How the animals groan! The herds of livestock are perplexed, because they have no pasture. Yes, the flocks of sheep are made desolate.
units.rightText: How the cattle groan! The herds wander in confusion because they have no pasture. Even the flocks of sheep are suffering.

units.leftText: LORD, I cry to you, for the fire has devoured the pastures of the wilderness, and the flame has burned all the trees of the field.
units.rightText: To You, O LORD, I call, for fire has consumed the open pastures and flames have scorched all the trees of the field.

units.leftText: Yes, the animals of the field pant to you, for the water brooks have dried up, and the fire has devoured the pastures of the wilderness.
units.rightText: Even the beasts of the field pant for You, for the streams of water have dried up, and fire has consumed the open pastures.

units.leftText: Blow the trumpet in Zion, and sound an alarm in my holy mountain! Let all the inhabitants of the land tremble, for the day of the LORD comes, for it is close at hand:
units.rightText: Blow the ram’s horn in Zion; sound the alarm on My holy mountain! Let all who dwell in the land tremble, for the Day of the LORD is coming; indeed, it is near—

units.leftText: A day of darkness and gloominess, a day of clouds and thick darkness. As the dawn spreading on the mountains, a great and strong people; there has never been the like, neither will there be any more after them, even to the years of many generations.
units.rightText: a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and blackness. Like the dawn overspreading the mountains a great and strong army appears, such as never was of old, nor will ever be in ages to come.

units.leftText: A fire devours before them, and behind them, a flame burns. The land is as the garden of Eden before them, and behind them, a desolate wilderness. Yes, and no one has escaped them.
units.rightText: Before them a fire devours, and behind them a flame scorches. The land before them is like the Garden of Eden, but behind them, it is like a desert wasteland — surely nothing will escape them.

units.leftText: Their appearance is as the appearance of horses, and they run as horsemen.
units.rightText: Their appearance is like that of horses, and they gallop like swift steeds.
rightNotes: 2:4 Or like charioteers or like cavalry

units.leftText: Like the noise of chariots on the tops of the mountains, they leap, like the noise of a flame of fire that devours the stubble, like a strong people set in battle array.
units.rightText: With a sound like that of chariots they bound over the mountaintops, like the crackling of fire consuming stubble, like a mighty army deployed for battle.

units.leftText: At their presence the peoples are in anguish. All faces have grown pale.
units.rightText: Nations writhe in horror before them; every face turns pale.

units.leftText: They run like mighty men. They climb the wall like warriors. They each march in his line, and they don’t swerve off course.
units.rightText: They charge like mighty men; they scale the walls like men of war. Each one marches in formation, not swerving from the course.

units.leftText: One doesn’t jostle another. They each march in their own path. They burst through the defenses and don’t break ranks.
units.rightText: They do not jostle one another; each proceeds in his path. They burst through the defenses, never breaking ranks.

units.leftText: They rush on the city. They run on the wall. They climb up into the houses. They enter in at the windows like thieves.
units.rightText: They storm the city; they run along the wall; they climb into houses, entering through windows like thieves.

units.leftText: The earth quakes before them. The heavens tremble. The sun and the moon are darkened, and the stars withdraw their shining.
units.rightText: Before them the earth quakes; the heavens tremble. The sun and moon grow dark, and the stars lose their brightness.

units.leftText: The LORD thunders his voice before his army, for his forces are very great; for he is strong who obeys his command; for the day of the LORD is great and very awesome, and who can endure it?
units.rightText: The LORD raises His voice in the presence of His army. Indeed, His camp is very large, for mighty are those who obey His command. For the Day of the LORD is great and very dreadful. Who can endure it? Return with All Your Heart

units.leftText: “Yet even now,” says the LORD, “turn to me with all your heart, and with fasting, and with weeping, and with mourning.”
units.rightText: “Yet even now,” declares the LORD, “return to Me with all your heart, with fasting, weeping, and mourning.”

units.leftText: Tear your heart and not your garments, and turn to the LORD, your God; for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, and relents from sending calamity.
units.rightText: So rend your hearts and not your garments, and return to the LORD your God. For He is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion. And He relents from sending disaster.
rightNotes: 2:13 Forms of the Hebrew chesed are translated here and in most cases throughout the Scriptures as loving devotion; the range of meaning includes love, goodness, kindness, faithfulness, and mercy, as well as loyalty to a covenant.

units.leftText: Who knows? He may turn and relent, and leave a blessing behind him, even a meal offering and a drink offering to the LORD, your God.
units.rightText: Who knows? He may turn and relent and leave a blessing behind Him — grain and drink offerings for the LORD your God.

units.leftText: Blow the trumpet in Zion! Sanctify a fast. Call a solemn assembly.
units.rightText: Blow the ram’s horn in Zion, consecrate a fast, proclaim a sacred assembly.

units.leftText: Gather the people. Sanctify the assembly. Assemble the elders. Gather the children, and those who nurse from breasts. Let the bridegroom go out of his room, and the bride out of her chamber.
units.rightText: Gather the people, sanctify the congregation, assemble the aged, gather the children, even those nursing at the breast. Let the bridegroom leave his room, and the bride her chamber.

units.leftText: Let the priests, the ministers of the LORD, weep between the porch and the altar, and let them say, “Spare your people, LORD, and don’t give your heritage to reproach, that the nations should rule over them. Why should they say among the peoples, ‘Where is their God?’”
units.rightText: Let the priests who minister before the LORD weep between the portico and the altar, saying, “Spare Your people, O LORD, and do not make Your heritage a reproach, an object of scorn among the nations. Why should they say among the peoples, ‘Where is their God?’” Restoration Promised

units.leftText: Then the LORD was jealous for his land, and had pity on his people.
units.rightText: Then the LORD became jealous for His land, and He spared His people.

units.leftText: The LORD answered his people, “Behold, I will send you grain, new wine, and oil, and you will be satisfied with them; and I will no more make you a reproach among the nations.
units.rightText: And the LORD answered His people: “Behold, I will send you grain, new wine, and oil, and by them you will be satisfied. I will never again make you a reproach among the nations.
leftNotes: 2:19 “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה*”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.

units.leftText: But I will remove the northern army far away from you, and will drive it into a barren and desolate land, its front into the eastern sea, and its back into the western sea; and its stench will come up, and its bad smell will rise.” Surely he has done great things.
units.rightText: The northern army I will drive away from you, banishing it to a barren and desolate land, its front ranks into the Eastern Sea, and its rear guard into the Western Sea. And its stench will rise; its foul odor will ascend. For He has done great things.
rightNotes: 2:20 That is, the Mediterranean Sea, also called the Great Sea

units.leftText: Land, don’t be afraid. Be glad and rejoice, for the LORD has done great things.
units.rightText: Do not be afraid, O land; rejoice and be glad, for the LORD has done great things.

units.leftText: Don’t be afraid, you animals of the field; for the pastures of the wilderness spring up, for the tree bears its fruit. The fig tree and the vine yield their strength.
units.rightText: Do not be afraid, O beasts of the field, for the open pastures have turned green, the trees bear their fruit, and the fig tree and vine yield their best.

units.leftText: “Be glad then, you children of Zion, and rejoice in the LORD, your God; for he gives you the early rain in just measure, and he causes the rain to come down for you, the early rain and the latter rain, as before.
units.rightText: Be glad, O children of Zion, and rejoice in the LORD your God, for He has given you the autumn rains for your vindication. He sends you showers, both autumn and spring rains, as before.

units.leftText: The threshing floors will be full of wheat, and the vats will overflow with new wine and oil.
units.rightText: The threshing floors will be full of grain, and the vats will overflow with new wine and oil.

units.leftText: I will restore to you the years that the swarming locust has eaten, the great locust, the grasshopper, and the caterpillar, my great army, which I sent among you.
units.rightText: I will repay you for the years eaten by locusts — the swarming locust, the young locust, the destroying locust, and the devouring locust — My great army that I sent against you.
rightNotes: 2:25 The precise identification of the four kinds of insects mentioned here is uncertain.

units.leftText: You will have plenty to eat and be satisfied, and will praise the name of the LORD, your God, who has dealt wondrously with you; and my people will never again be disappointed.
units.rightText: You will have plenty to eat, until you are satisfied. You will praise the name of the LORD your God, who has worked wonders for you. My people will never again be put to shame.

units.leftText: You will know that I am among Israel, and that I am the LORD, your God, and there is no one else; and my people will never again be disappointed.
units.rightText: Then you will know that I am present in Israel and that I am the LORD your God, and there is no other. My people will never again be put to shame. I Will Pour Out My Spirit (Acts 2:14–36|ACT 2:14-36*)

units.leftText: “It will happen afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your old men will dream dreams. Your young men will see visions.
units.rightText: And afterward, I will pour out My Spirit on all people. Your sons and daughters will prophesy, your old men will dream dreams, your young men will see visions.

units.leftText: And also on the servants and on the handmaids in those days, I will pour out my Spirit.
units.rightText: Even on My menservants and maidservants, I will pour out My Spirit in those days.

units.leftText: I will show wonders in the heavens and on the earth: blood, fire, and pillars of smoke.
units.rightText: I will show wonders in the heavens and on the earth, blood and fire and columns of smoke.

units.leftText: The sun will be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and terrible day of the LORD comes.
units.rightText: The sun will be turned to darkness and the moon to blood before the coming of the great and awesome Day of the LORD.

units.leftText: It will happen that whoever will call on the LORD’s name shall be saved; for in Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be those who escape, as the LORD has said, and among the remnant, those whom the LORD calls.
units.rightText: And everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will be saved; for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be deliverance, as the LORD has promised, among the remnant called by the LORD.[’’]

units.leftText: “For, behold, in those days, and in that time, when I restore the fortunes of Judah and Jerusalem,
units.rightText: “Yes, in those days and at that time, when I restore Judah and Jerusalem from captivity,
rightNotes: 3:1 Or restore the fortunes of Judah and Jerusalem

units.leftText: I will gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat; and I will execute judgment on them there for my people, and for my heritage, Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations. They have divided my land,
units.rightText: I will gather all the nations and bring them down to the Valley of Jehoshaphat. There I will enter into judgment against them concerning My people, My inheritance, Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations as they divided up My land.
rightNotes: 3:2 Jehoshaphat means the LORD judges; also in verse 12.

units.leftText: and have cast lots for my people, and have given a boy for a prostitute, and sold a girl for wine, that they may drink.
units.rightText: They cast lots for My people; they bartered a boy for a prostitute and sold a girl for wine to drink.

units.leftText: “Yes, and what are you to me, Tyre and Sidon, and all the regions of Philistia? Will you repay me? And if you repay me, I will swiftly and speedily return your repayment on your own head.
units.rightText: Now what do you have against Me, O Tyre, Sidon, and all the regions of Philistia? Are you rendering against Me a recompense? If you retaliate against Me, I will swiftly and speedily return your recompense upon your heads.

units.leftText: Because you have taken my silver and my gold, and have carried my finest treasures into your temples,
units.rightText: For you took My silver and gold and carried off My finest treasures to your temples.

units.leftText: and have sold the children of Judah and the children of Jerusalem to the sons of the Greeks, that you may remove them far from their border.
units.rightText: You sold the people of Judah and Jerusalem to the Greeks, to send them far from their homeland.
rightNotes: 3:6 Or to the peoples of Javan

units.leftText: Behold, I will stir them up out of the place where you have sold them, and will return your repayment on your own head;
units.rightText: Behold, I will rouse them from the places to which you sold them; I will return your recompense upon your heads.

units.leftText: and I will sell your sons and your daughters into the hands of the children of Judah, and they will sell them to the men of Sheba, to a faraway nation, for the LORD has spoken it.”
units.rightText: I will sell your sons and daughters into the hands of the people of Judah, and they will sell them to the Sabeans — to a distant nation.” Indeed, the LORD has spoken.

units.leftText: Proclaim this among the nations: “Prepare for war! Stir up the mighty men. Let all the warriors draw near. Let them come up.
units.rightText: Proclaim this among the nations: “Prepare for war; rouse the mighty men; let all the men of war advance and attack!

units.leftText: Beat your plowshares into swords, and your pruning hooks into spears. Let the weak say, ‘I am strong.’
units.rightText: Beat your plowshares into swords and your pruning hooks into spears. Let the weak say, ‘I am strong!’

units.leftText: Hurry and come, all you surrounding nations, and gather yourselves together.” Cause your mighty ones to come down there, LORD.
units.rightText: Come quickly, all you surrounding nations, and gather yourselves. Bring down Your mighty ones, O LORD.

units.leftText: “Let the nations arouse themselves, and come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat; for there I will sit to judge all the surrounding nations.
units.rightText: Let the nations be roused and advance to the Valley of Jehoshaphat, for there I will sit down to judge all the nations on every side.

units.leftText: Put in the sickle; for the harvest is ripe. Come, tread, for the wine press is full, the vats overflow, for their wickedness is great.”
units.rightText: Swing the sickle, for the harvest is ripe. Come, trample the grapes, for the winepress is full; the wine vats overflow because their wickedness is great.
rightNotes: 3:13 LXX the harvest has come; see also Mark 4:29|MRK 4:29*.

units.leftText: Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision! For the day of the LORD is near in the valley of decision.
units.rightText: Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision! For the Day of the LORD is near in the valley of decision.

units.leftText: The sun and the moon are darkened, and the stars withdraw their shining.
units.rightText: The sun and moon will grow dark, and the stars will no longer shine.

units.leftText: The LORD will roar from Zion, and thunder from Jerusalem; and the heavens and the earth will shake; but the LORD will be a refuge to his people, and a stronghold to the children of Israel.
units.rightText: The LORD will roar from Zion and raise His voice from Jerusalem; heaven and earth will tremble. But the LORD will be a refuge for His people, a stronghold for the people of Israel. Blessings for God’s People

units.leftText: “So you will know that I am the LORD, your God, dwelling in Zion, my holy mountain. Then Jerusalem will be holy, and no strangers will pass through her any more.
units.rightText: Then you will know that I am the LORD your God, who dwells in Zion, My holy mountain. Jerusalem will be holy, never again to be overrun by foreigners.

units.leftText: It will happen in that day, that the mountains will drop down sweet wine, the hills will flow with milk, all the brooks of Judah will flow with waters; and a fountain will flow out from the LORD’s house, and will water the valley of Shittim.
units.rightText: And in that day the mountains will drip with sweet wine, and the hills will flow with milk. All the streams of Judah will run with water, and a spring will flow from the house of the LORD to water the Valley of Acacias.

units.leftText: Egypt will be a desolation and Edom will be a desolate wilderness, for the violence done to the children of Judah, because they have shed innocent blood in their land.
units.rightText: Egypt will become desolate, and Edom a desert wasteland, because of the violence done to the people of Judah, in whose land they shed innocent blood.

units.leftText: But Judah will be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.
units.rightText: But Judah will be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.

units.leftText: I will cleanse their blood that I have not cleansed, for the LORD dwells in Zion.”
units.rightText: For I will avenge their blood, which I have not yet avenged. ” For the LORD dwells in Zion.
rightNotes: 3:21 Or For I will pardon their bloodguilt, which I have not yet pardoned.
